analysis: Examined SSDPrefixCache.swift base lines 1256-2193; the only change (base 1790-1799, head 1790-1800) adds an optional `unusedSince: Int64?` parameter to retireOwnedEntries/retireIndexedEntries and forwards it to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove. The default is nil, so existing callers keep their prior behavior. Internal callers that pass no value are unchanged: evictOldestEntry (base 1780), sweepExpiredEntries (base 1855) and retireOwnedEntries' callers. Removal still runs under removalLock and still requires hasSafeRoot and ownsEvictionRoot. The epochStore binding and externalChange reconciliation are preserved. The parameter appears intended as a last-access guard, so retirement would skip entries touched after a snapshot. That would narrow deletions (for example against a race with the stage() touch at base 1579-1586) rather than widen them. Relevant threat: T-041 (TTL/LRU sweep, at-rest bound, epoch semantics); nothing in it relates to HMAC naming, AAD, KEK handling or staging reservations. Uncertainty for integration: SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove's handling of unusedSince is not supplied. Integration should verify three things: (1) nil preserves the prior semantics exactly; (2) a non-nil value only skips entries whose index lastAccess exceeds it and never removes extra files; (3) skipped entries do not desync the index or byte accounting. The external caller supplying unusedSince (likely box-wide eviction or a cross-store sweep) is also not visible. If it only skips, TTL enforcement could extend while an entry stays in active use, which is consistent with the sliding TTL. No regression was identified from the visible source.
